open_risks: GET /health, GET /health/ready and POST /v1/requests are implemented and tested but not yet frozen through a joint two-person contract PR review — mark frozen@0.1.0 once both engineers have signed off. Contract version was 0.3.0 vs CHANGELOG.md's 0.1.0 (a real inconsistency, since fixed to 0.1.0 on both sides).

GET /health/ready is permitAll at the Spring Security layer, matching the manual's own reference implementation; it still needs to be kept off the public internet at the infra/WAF layer before staging is exposed (see docs/security/threat-model.md).

AWS staging is deferred (ADR-004) — no budget available right now, even for the near-$0/month minimal design in docs/runbooks/aws-staging-setup.md. The Phase 0 connected checkpoint uses a cloudflared Quick Tunnel instead; revisit AWS no later than Phase 3, when Twilio needs a stable (non-rotating) webhook URL a Quick Tunnel can't provide.

Backend has no Redis dependency or Redis readiness check, even though infra/compose.yml and docker-compose.yml provision Redis. Either wire it in when something actually needs it, or drop it from Compose — don't let 'provisioned but unused' stand as if it were tested.
PRODUCT_BUNDLE_IDENTIFIER changed to com.abubakarsidiq01.plug.app101 (com.plug.app was already claimed by another Apple account) and committed to project.pbxproj.

docs/onboarding/windows.md had real bugs (no root Gradle wrapper — backend is a standalone Gradle project, not a :backend subproject; the bru CLI was never actually installed, only the GUI app; <org> placeholder never filled in; wrong tests/api path) — fixed, and .github/workflows/windows-onboarding-check.yml now runs the literal documented commands on a real windows-latest GitHub Actions runner on every push/PR. This validates the commands work on real Windows infrastructure but does not replace person_two (@uzom-a) actually running through it once herself (manual P0.S1-two) — CI can't validate the interactive parts (Docker Desktop's install wizard, WSL2 setup, trust prompts).
docs/design/figma-implementation-checklist.md exists as a checklist document, not linked to an actual Figma file — no Figma access was available this session.

The G0 gate itself cannot be signed by automation: manual.docx §4.3/§27.1 requires a live, two-person connected checkpoint against real staging with a physical iPhone — that is the one remaining step that is inherently not automatable.
